newsitem.title: GERMANY: OECD urges further reform on German health care.
newsitem.headline: OECD urges further reform on German health care.

text.p: The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development on Tuesday urged Germany to take further steps to reform its health care system so as to approve cost efficiency and improve financing.

The OECD said in a special study in its annual report on Germany that problems such as consumer behaviour patterns which led to overuse of the health system in some areas and inefficient use in other areas had to be tackled.
The lack of contribution by patients to medical fees for consultations, for example, meant that people were more likely to visit a doctor even for minor ailments, it said.

Hospitals had to be reformed to ensure they provided cost-effective services and changes needed to be made to encourage synergies within the medical profession, where remuneration links to numbers of patients often made a doctor reluctant to refer cases on to another practitioner.
This reluctance to refer cases often led to an unnecessarily high number of hospital treatments, he said.

Heavy restrictions governing pharmacies tended to boost prices for medication and prevent normal market forces taking effect, it added, urging Bonn to "liberalise the ownership of pharmacies to permit the development of chains and more actively promote the use of parallel imports."
A more competitive environment should also be set up between statutory health funds, allowing them to become active purchasers of health care, the OECD said.

The think-tank praised reforms earlier in the 1990's which they sadi had come some way toward breaking down rigidities and inconsistencies in health care structures but warned that the reforms had not gone far enough.

"Further policy initiatives are needed to i) improve incentives for households to use health care ecoonomically and to place more emphasis on prevention, ii) provide incentives for health suppliers to reduce costs in a sustainable manner; and iii) strengthen the integration of the health system both between the ambulatory and stationary sectors as well as between the health insurance system and the rehabilitation and long term care sectors," it concluded.
